Hi Guys,

Have a played this wrongly? Is this a type of trade you guys would take or are there reasons I should not have taken this?

Look forward to your comments and criticism.

AHA, I´ve noticed you guys started talking about PAZ´s.

However, I´d like to comment on my trading. I´ve been trading before I discovered this method and this forum, so I had prior experience and was able to see the zones and the pricea action fairly quickly. So, I didn´t take long and I saw those zones and the price action we´re looking for all over the chart and began realizing how price moved ( which is a good thing I suppose ). My account grew fast.

However, since I started seeing the zones everywhere I began to take probably far too many of them. And since the beginning of last week I got whipped. I got whipped badly. I was able to get some back and I think now´s the time to realize what happened. Sound familiar?

Also, I have to ask again about trend. I know it has been touched several times here and trend seems still somewhat confusing to me when trading S/D. (Some of my best thoughts come in bed before falling asleep. Maybe I should actually write them down as they say, so maybe I could have avoided being whipped. How about a thread where people post there thoughts about trading before fallin asleep?)

I´d say when trading S/D there is not really a trend to follow? Since we´re looking for engulfs of critical areas there is only be an engulf of an important level either to the nort or south in any given time frame.

However, on the other hand I have to say that if a currency pair is strongly bullish (clear trend for example on the daily) one does not really trade against that, but how can I incorporate that into my trading. Would i only be looking for engulfs north in this example?

It´s a long one I know, but it had to be done. I´m looking forward to thoughts and opinions.

I believe these are valid points. You find out painfully quick with S and D levels if they are wrong (especially when there is a strong trend) - even if they tick every box on what a good level is supposed to look like. I am still finding PAZ very subjective and I have seen many seemingly good levels engulfed that make absolutely no difference to where price goes. There is always an explanation for a good trade and a bad one... just look left until you find one. I know there are a select few here that are consistently profitable, but it is a difficult approach to master due to the amount of interpretative analyses involved. I know indicators are discounted here, but it does smooth out a lot of subjectivity and provides for more consistent (albeit later) decision making. I think every trader is different - skills, personality etc that may not ultimately favour pure PA decision making. For some, blending both may the best solution for them. I am finding myself falling into that camp to be honest. FWIW

Hey Hotochin,

i look for High and Low price, i search for decision points, i ask myself which level people think that will hold (so there are lots of SL behind it) - which is very attractive for FO. I try to think in terms of order-flow as much as i can. Where are the buyers, seller? How would you fill 1mio € into long/short? Where is price on the HTF. What is price doing? Where can liquidity be found? (cous there is where mostly big money get their orders in - so they dont leave a too big impact)

Currently i try to get more into psychological part of the game, rather than pattern recognition.

Hope that helps.
